business.description: Arrow Greentech Ltd. is India's largest manufacturer of water-soluble films (Watersol® brand) and bio-compostable solutions, and manufactures anti-counterfeit products, security elements, and security films for document, brand, and high-security applications. Through subsidiary Avery Pharmaceuticals, it develops novel drug delivery systems (mouth-dissolving and oral thin-film products) and undertakes contract development and manufacturing of nutraceutical and pharmaceutical products.

outlook.statement: Priorities: scale green products business through new capacity and applications; convert deep IP pipeline into next generation of security solutions and related business verticals; grow Avery toward regulated markets through partnerships and approvals; expand international footprint.
Variability of a single year does not define franchise built on patents, proprietary technology and fortress balance sheet; it is a feature of the high-value model deliberately chosen.
Business outlook and future prospects of the Company is discussed in detail in Management Discussion and Analysis Report attached herewith.

Company is well positioned to leverage opportunities across both segments; Green Products segment 52% growth during the year from a small base; regulatory pull from Extended Producer Responsibility framework and recycled-content mandates; High-tech Products segment benefiting from counterfeiting concerns and serialisation mandates; debt-free balance sheet provides capacity to fund Dahej expansion and R&D

IMF projects global growth of 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027; India real GDP grew 7.6% in FY 2025-26; RBI repo rate at 5.25% with neutral stance; FY 2026-27 real GDP growth projection 6.9%, CPI inflation projection 4.6%

Elevated energy prices and the inflation outlook raise the risk of higher PVA and other input costs, while currency volatility affects both export realisations and imported input costs. Importation of non-standard materials, including extruded films from China, continues to pressure competitive pricing in mass-market segments. Working capital employed increased during the year, reflecting movement in receivables and inventory, and its normalisation continues to be a management focus.
The Group continues to monitor the finalisation of State Rules and clarifications from the Government on other aspects of the Labour Codes and would make appropriate adjustments, if needed.
